q: In the Next.js App Router, what is a page or layout by default?
options: A static HTML file with no React
why: Layouts and pages are Server Components by default. You opt in to the browser with "use client".

q: Every component under a file with "use client" needs its own "use client" line.
why: No. The directive marks the entry to the browser side. Its imports and the components it renders directly join the client bundle automatically.

q: What does the browser receive when a Server Component runs?
options: The result, as an RSC payload
The source code of the component
why: The server runs the component and sends the finished result. The code, the query and the secrets stay on the server.

q: Which of these can be passed as props from a Server Component to a Client Component?
why: Props must be serializable. Strings, dates and plain objects work. A normal function cannot be turned into plain data, so it cannot cross. Only Server Actions can.

q: A client Modal must show a cart that reads the database. How do you keep the cart on the server?
options: Pass <Cart /> to Modal as children from a Server Component
why: A component passed as children is rendered on the server and dropped into the slot. If Modal imports Cart, Cart joins the client bundle.

q: Which npm package makes the build fail if a file with secrets is imported into a Client Component? (one word with a hyphen)
why: import 'server-only' at the top of the file turns the mistake into a build error instead of a bug in production.
